framing: Two dedup arms, BOTH byte-gated. Arm R (rebuild-dedup, gen-rebuild) = incremental reuse-ACROSS-CHANGE: a localized single-host edit recomputes only that host and skips the untouched hosts, byte-identical to a full rebuild (resultEqualsFullRebuild). Its saving = the SKIPPED hosts baseline-composition counters — NOT a single-eval speedup (gen-rebuild does not beat O(|cone|) in one pure eval). Arm C (class-share, den s1/s2) = a config-RESOLUTION optimization: byte-identical terminal (SOUND) but NO composition win in this SEPARATE-per-host-eval harness — a consistent ~+4% s2 machinery overhead. The Plane-2a ~60% prior is a CROSS-HOST fleet-eval-sharing collapse that separate per-host evals cannot capture (reconciled, not reproduced). See MEASUREMENT.md. Arm C's TERMINAL-plane (pessimal) cost — den@s2's machinery overhead when forcing toplevel.drvPath, on a byte-identical terminal — is pinned in class-share.terminalPessimal (an overhead/soundness record, NOT a win; no floor).
pinNote: Deterministic evaluator counters (verified reproduced across two runs) + digests are EXACT. gcTotalBytes/cpuTime omitted (informational). The class-share secondary cfg.config witness is INFORMATIONAL: builtins.tryEval CANNOT catch its terminating stack overflow, so it measures work-up-to-a-deterministic-crash — the DELTA is stable and reported, absolutes are a crash-prefix, never gated. PREAMBLE SENSITIVITY: the composition counters here come from the fleet-stats driver baked-store-path preamble; nrFunctionCalls/nrPrimOpCalls + the digest are preamble-invariant, but nrOpUpdateValuesCopied/nrThunks shift ±1-2 under a different preamble — a reader reproducing OUT-OF-BAND via the README github-getFlake command WILL see ±2 on those two counters (same as g6-split.json stub provenance). The reported class-share DELTAS (s2 − pinned) and Arm R saving are computed WITHIN one preamble (the driver), so they are exact and preamble-invariant. class-share.terminalPessimal: both terminal forces (pinned + s2) are measured in ONE out-of-band preamble (class-share-toplevel-pessimal.sh, x2 STOP-on-diff) so its s2-pinned delta is BIT-EXACT within-preamble; its `pinned` terminal counters therefore differ from g6-split baseline-toplevel by the +-1-3 out-of-band preamble wobble (fcalls +1 / copies +2 / thunks +3), while its terminalDrvPath is byte-identical (the byte gate).

pins._meta: underscore-prefixed keys are prose annotations, not revs; consumers skip them. den-s1/s2 are LOCAL-ONLY worktree branches (git+file://, campaign impure-local by design); gen-rebuild is public (github:sini/gen-rebuild).

rebuild-dedup.mechanism: Model the fleet as a gen-rebuild graph: nodes = a shared class-composition producer + the fleet hosts; edge host->shared (gen-graph edges id = deps of id). recompute(host) forces the host REAL compositionNames folded with its node data + the shared value. build = full store; propagateEager {host=edit} = incremental. Helper: hola.adapter.fleetRebuildSoundness.

byteGate.note: resultEqualsFullRebuild = propagateEager store byte-identical to a from-scratch build with the same edit (re-asserted on the REAL corpus). coneOnlyRecompute proven by a POISONED recompute that throws on the untouched hosts and is never called. digest = sha256 of the full soundness record (reproduced across two runs).

savedRecompute.source: sum of baseline-composition counters over the skipped hosts ["blade","cortex"] (from g6-split.json)

pessimalSharedEdit.note: Editing the SHARED node moves every host hash -> cone = the whole graph -> dedup saves nothing. The honest boundary.

rebuild-dedup.crossPlaneNote: The savedRecompute counters (35,350,336 fcalls = blade+cortex) are the SEPARATE-per-host (deploy-time / cross-eval) recompute. The class-share keystone shows the SAME declaration layer is nearly free to share WITHIN one eval (blade+cortex = 18.8M ≈ 1.066× a single host, not the 35.35M naive sum) — different execution planes, NOT in tension: Arm R saves the cross-eval recompute a change repeats host-by-host; class-share measures the in-eval plane where native Nix memoization already shares it. See MEASUREMENT.md §Arm-C reconciliation pt2.

class-share.mechanism: Re-run the fleet with nc.inputs.den overridden pinned(5df0987) -> s2(487cc671). s1/s2 share per-sid/class composition work across hosts of a class. Measured per-host: compositionNames under s2 vs pinned; the terminal drvPath must stay byte-identical.
class-share.verdict: BYTE-SOUND, NO measurable composition win in the per-host harness (+~4.6% s2 machinery overhead, host-invariant). The class-share win is a CROSS-HOST fleet-eval-sharing collapse (Plane-2a ~60% prior) that separate per-host evals cannot capture; the derivation-free composition witness sits at the declaration layer, which native Nix thunk-memoization already shares. Reconciled in MEASUREMENT.md.

compositionDigest.note: s2 composition digest (top-level option-name list) == pinned per host: the class-share declaration surface is unchanged (resolution-only optimization).

toplevelDrvPath.note: s2 system.build.toplevel.drvPath == pinned per host: the TERMINAL is byte-identical. A class-share arm that moved the drvPath would be a BUG, not a win.

compositionWitness.note: options-declaration walk (baseline-composition). delta = s2 - pinned; POSITIVE = s2 OVERHEAD, not a win. Deterministic (reproduced across two runs).

secondaryWitness.note: tryEval-guarded cfg.config deepSeq (INFORMATIONAL — see pinNote; terminates via an uncatchable stack overflow, work-up-to-crash). Same conclusion as the primary: consistent ~+0.81M-fcall s2 overhead, no win.

terminalPessimal.note: PESSIMAL-plane (terminal / system.build.toplevel.drvPath) cost record for den@s2. The terminal is derivation-storm-dominated (g6-split: composition is only ~5% of the terminal //-storm), so den@s2 per-host machinery (pipe.reads cone-expander + per-sid hostConfigFor) is paid in FULL while the cross-host sharing s2 targets cannot manifest in this separate-per-host harness. delta = s2 - pinned; POSITIVE = OVERHEAD on a BYTE-IDENTICAL terminal (terminalDrvPath unchanged — see byteGate.toplevelDrvPath; a class-share arm that MOVED the drvPath would be a BUG, not a win) → this is an overhead/soundness record, NOT a win, so there is NO floor. Both forces measured in ONE out-of-band preamble (ci/bench/class-share-toplevel-pessimal.sh, x2 STOP-on-diff) so delta is BIT-EXACT within-preamble (secondaryWitness discipline). The `pinned` terminal is re-measured HERE for that exactness, NOT read from g6-split; its drvPath == g6-split baseline-toplevel (the byte gate) and its counters match g6-split baseline-toplevel within the +-1-3 out-of-band preamble wobble (pinNote).
